01 / Project definition

Objective and engineering context

The assembly is framed as a generic avionics mounting support for a small uncrewed aircraft or aerospace test platform. The supported item is treated as an idealized avionics unit rather than a specific real product.

Objectives

  • Create a portfolio-ready structural assembly model with a mounting plate and two support brackets.
  • Represent the equipment mass and its load transfer using idealized finite-element connections.
  • Run a linear static gravity case and check global force equilibrium.
  • Assess sensitivity to mesh refinement.
  • Run normal-mode analysis and assess frequency stability.
  • Compare the baseline with a thinner-plate variant and a cutout variant.
  • Use MAC matrices to compare mode shapes between configurations.
02 / Model & methodology

Geometry, material and FE idealization

The mounting plate and bracket parts are represented using shell elements. HyperMesh was used for preprocessing, property/material assignment and mesh-quality checks.

03 / Loads & connections

Equipment mass, gravity and constraints

A 2 kg electronics mass is represented using a CONM2 concentrated mass. The mass is placed at the centre node of an RBE3 connection that distributes the equipment load into the mounting plate. Gravity is 9810 mm/s².

ConfigurationMassGravityGravity force
Baseline13.480 kg9810 mm/s²132238.8 kg·mm/s² = 132.24 N
Reduced thickness12.427 kg9810 mm/s²121908.9 kg·mm/s² = 121.91 N
Cutout12.867 kg9810 mm/s²126225.3 kg·mm/s² = 126.23 N

For the no-washer model, all six degrees of freedom are constrained at the bolt-location support nodes. A washer/modified-connection model uses an RBE2 representation at the hole region.

04 / Static analysis

Mesh convergence — SOL 101

Linear static analysis was performed using MSC Nastran SOL 101. Displacement is reported in mm and stress in MPa. Applied gravity load and SPC reaction were checked for equilibrium.

MeshElementsNodesApplied loadSPC reactionMax displacementNon-local VM
10 mm1,3401,404−132.24 N+132.24 N0.004918 mm0.6303 MPa
7.5 mm1,9612,152−132.24 N+132.24 N0.004922 mm0.6306 MPa
5 mm2,6382,884−132.24 N+132.24 N0.004925 mm0.6311 MPa

The 5 mm full-model peak von Mises stress was 0.666 MPa, higher than the isolated/non-local value because the refined mesh resolved a localized connection-region peak.

Interpretation: Global displacement and the consistently extracted non-local stress changed only slightly with refinement. The localized connection stress is more mesh-sensitive and should be considered separately.

06 / Geometry sensitivity

Thickness and cutout variants

MetricBaselineThin plateCutout
Total mass13.480 kg12.427 kg (−7.8%)12.867 kg (−4.5%)
Gravity load132.24 N121.91 N (−7.8%)126.23 N (−4.5%)
Max displacement0.004925 mm0.011500 mm (+133.5%)0.004972 mm (+1.0%)
Full-model peak VM0.666 MPa1.320 MPa (+98.2%)0.682 MPa (+2.4%)
Non-local VM0.631 MPa1.120 MPa (+77.5%)0.679 MPa (+7.6%)

The thin configuration reduces mass but substantially increases displacement and stress under the model's own gravity load. The cutout configuration gives a smaller mass reduction with only a small change in maximum displacement for the reported self-weight case.

These are self-weight comparisons. A controlled stiffness sensitivity study would use the same externally applied force/moment and identical boundary conditions across variants.

07 / Mode-shape correlation

Modal Assurance Criterion (MAC)

MAC was evaluated using concatenated X, Y and Z displacement components for matched nodes. The comparison uses a consistent node/component order and only common nodes where the cutout variant removes nodes.

MAC equation

MACᵢⱼ = |φᵢᵀψⱼ|² / [(φᵢᵀφᵢ)(ψⱼᵀψⱼ)]

The report states that the matrices use displacement components from the .fo6 file and are rounded to four decimal places. Rows are modes from the second-named model and columns are modes from the first-named model.

08 / Engineering discussion

What the study demonstrates

  • Mesh convergence: Global displacement and modal frequencies are stable across the 10, 7.5 and 5 mm baseline meshes, while local connection stress is more refinement-sensitive.
  • Thickness sensitivity: Reducing plate thickness reduces mass by 7.8% but increases maximum displacement by 133.5% and full-model peak von Mises stress by 98.2% for the self-weight case.
  • Cutout sensitivity: The cutout configuration reduces mass by 4.5% with a 1.0% increase in maximum displacement in the reported self-weight case.
  • Connection sensitivity: The washer/modified-connection model changes both the connection representation and the resulting response, so it is treated as a connection-modelling sensitivity rather than a pure geometry comparison.
  • Modal behaviour: MAC shows strong correlation for several corresponding modes while some higher modes exhibit cross-mode correlation after geometry changes.
09 / Conclusion

Complete CAE workflow

This project combines finite-element model preparation, linear static analysis, normal-mode analysis, mesh convergence, geometry sensitivity and MAC-based mode-shape correlation in one documented workflow.

The baseline static study showed maximum displacement changing only from 0.004918 mm at 10 mm mesh size to 0.004925 mm at 5 mm. The non-local stress measure remained nearly unchanged, while the refined mesh better resolved the localized connection-region peak.

The lightweighting study demonstrates the trade-off between mass and structural response under self-weight. The report also shows why mode shape should be considered alongside frequency when comparing modal behaviour between design configurations.

Portfolio scope: This is a generic/idealized independent study. It is not a qualification analysis of real flight hardware and should not be interpreted as certification evidence.
